incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alerts: multiple gpu-node OOM/crash events detected across serving-pool-3. Aggregated anomaly: repeated CUDA illegal memory access + container restarts since 02:12 UTC. Auto-created thread for oncall handoff.

priya (oncall): saw the pager, jumping in. What's scope? any customer-facing endpoints degraded?

jordan (sre): impact: ~12% of requests to /v1/generate are getting 5xx over the last 6m, spikes correlate with GPU node flaps on gce-gpu-3*. Containers are exiting w/ SIGSEGV in runtime.

eli (runtime): stack trace from one container attached to node gce-gpu-3b: ```
E tensorflow: cuda illegal memory access at 0x7f8a3c000000
ServingRuntime: gpu_forward() +0x1a3
kv_cache: read_pagewalk()+0x5f
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```
We also see OOM killer logs in dmesg followed by NVRM GPU reset loops.

dana (eng): is this the same misaligned pagewalk pattern we saw last quarter or a new vector? any SMMU/pagetable hints?

eli (runtime): similar symptoms but different signature: the illegal access address is within the device addr window, read/write mismatch during a long multi-chunk prefix replay. Also seeing `pagewalk timeout` entries in kernel logs on a couple nodes. attaching snippet: ```
[ 4021.123456] nvidia: Copy Engine Timeout
[ 4021.123480] deviceaddr: pagewalk failed, unaligned ptr 0x7f8a3c05f000
[ 4021.123500] cuda: illegal memory access at 0x7f8a3c05f000
```

priya (oncall): good. immediate mitigation options? can we drain/cordon affected nodes and spin up fallback capacity?
\
jordan (sre): recommending: cordon gce-gpu-3b, gce-gpu-3c; drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Autoscaler should pick up new nodes in us-west1. I'll run `kubectl cordon` now.
\
elI (runtime): recommend runtime fallback to quantized model variant (cpu-backed or q4a) for in-flight canary traffic to reduce kernel memory pressure. Also enable `prefetch=false` on the loader config to reduce pagewalk bursts.
\
priya (oncall): @dana can you trigger rollback of latest runtime patch? this started ~02:09, was there a rolling kernel or runtime push?
\
dana (eng): I see a canary edge patch deployed 02:05 that touched page cache handling in the loader. Rolling that back now to previous revision (rev_2026_02_08). Will post progress.
\
ashley (support): customer inbound: a mid-market customer reported intermittent 500s and slow responses, offering ETA. Should we send interim notice?
\
priya (oncall): yes, send brief notification. Use cust-notify-bot draft: "We're investigating elevated 5xx for generation endpoints in us-west; mitigation in progress; no data loss; next update in 30m."
\
cust-notify-bot: Draft posted to #customer-updates. Sending after oncall approval.
\
jordan (sre): cordon/drain initiated. Affected pods are restarting but liveness probes failing quickly. Samples of `kubectl describe pod`: ```
Events:
  Warning  OOMKilled  3s  kubelet  Pod exceeded gpu memory and was OOMKilled
  Normal   BackOff    2s  kubelet  Back-off restarting failed container
```
\
eli (runtime): collecting full nvcrash dumps and container corefiles. Command I ran: ```
ssh gce-gpu-3b 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 && sudo /usr/local/bin/nvcrash_collect /var/log/nvcrash /tmp/nvcrash.tar.gz'```
I've uploaded artifacts to /incidents/1739456789/artifacts.tar.gz on the shared drive.
\
dana (eng): rollback applied to serving-runtime on canary tier. Monitoring for repro. If illegal access stops on drained nodes but continues on others, will escalate kernel team.
\
priya (oncall): rolling fallback policy to q4a is live for 10% traffic. Watch error budget and latency.
\
jordan (sre): early metrics: 10% drop in 5xx within 5m after cordon + rollback + fallback. However two other nodes show intermittent pagewalk errors — might be latent hardware ECC or driver regression.
\
eli (runtime): to triage, I need the exact CUDA driver version from failing nodes and compare with working nodes: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` — please paste outputs.
\
jordan (sre): gce-gpu-3b: 535.104; gce-gpu-4a (healthy): 535.104; so driver same. Kernel versions: 5.10.143 vs 5.10.141 on healthy. diffs in backports might matter.
\
dana (eng): raising to kernel-systems, attaching nvcrash + dmesg + core dumps. tagging @kernel-team.
\
priya (oncall): customer update sent: "Mitigations deployed (node cordon + runtime rollback + traffic fallback). We're seeing partial recovery; engineering continues root-cause triage. Next update in 30 minutes."
\
ashley (support): customers acknowledged. one asked for postmortem SLA; can we confirm expected timeline?
\
dana (eng): we'll have a preliminary RCA within 48 hours, full postmortem in 7 days.
\
eli (runtime): follow-ups: 1) collect full coredumps from all failed pods, 2) run memtest on suspect nodes overnight, 3) disable aggressive prefetch on loader by default until proven safe.
\
jordan (sre): created follow-up incident tasks: TASK-4432 (collect cores), TASK-4433 (node memtest), TASK-4434 (rollback audit).
\
priya (oncall): handing off to night oncall @jordan for monitoring. I'll re-open if regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
\
incident-bot: Incident thread closed for CRITICAL paging flaps after handoff. If new alerts fire, a new thread will be created."
